questions.question_text:
After a $16\%$ increase, a train fare is $\$29$.
Find the fare before the increase.

options.why: Took $16\%$ off $\$29$ instead of dividing by $116\%$; the old fare is not $84\%$ of the new one.
Increased $\$29$ by a further $16\%$ instead of working backwards.
Found $16\%$ of $\$29$, the size of the rise, rather than the original fare.

questions.question_text:
After a $40\%$ decrease, a flight ticket costs $\$276$.
Find the original price.

options.why: Added $40\%$ of $\$276$ instead of dividing by $60\%$; the original is not $140\%$ of the new price.
Took a further $40\%$ off $\$276$ instead of working backwards.
Found $40\%$ of $\$276$, the size of the drop, rather than the original price.

questions.question_text:
The number of daily passengers on a bus route fell by $30\%$, a drop of $42$ passengers.
How many passengers were there each day originally?

options.why: Treated the $42$ as the $70\%$ still travelling instead of as the $30\%$ lost.
Gave the number still travelling, which is $70\%$, rather than the original number.
Found $30\%$ of $42$ instead of scaling $42$ up from $30\%$ to $100\%$.

questions.solution_text:
The drop of $42$ passengers is the $30\%$ decrease.
$30\% = 42$
$1\% = 42 \div 30 = 1.4$
$100\% = 1.4 \times 100$
$= 140$ passengers

questions.question_text:
After a $12\%$ pay rise, a worker earns $\$168$ a day.
A student finds the original pay by taking $12\%$ off $\$168$, getting $\$147.84$.
Is this correct?

options.text: No; the original was $\$150$, because $\$168$ is $112\%$ of the original, not $100\%$.
Yes; taking $12\%$ off reverses a $12\%$ increase exactly.
options.why: A $12\%$ increase and a $12\%$ decrease act on different amounts, so they do not cancel.

options.text: No; the original was $\$188.16$, found by adding $12\%$ to $\$168$.
options.why: Adds another increase instead of working back to $100\%$.

options.text: Yes; $\$147.84$ is $88\%$ of $\$168$, which is the original.
options.why: The original is $100\%$ of itself, not $88\%$ of the increased value.

questions.question_text:
A hotel drops its nightly rate by $24\%$, so a room now costs $\$190$.
Find the rate before the drop.

options.why: Added $24\%$ of $\$190$ instead of dividing by $76\%$.
Took a further $24\%$ off $\$190$ instead of working backwards.
Found $24\%$ of $\$190$, the size of the drop, rather than the original rate.
Calculates 30% of £75 rather than finding the amount whose 30% is £75.
Uses an incorrect percentage multiplier and does not produce £75 at 30%.
Divides by 0.10 rather than by 0.30 when finding the whole.

questions.solution_text: Let the amount be $x$. Then $0.30x=75$, so $x=75/0.30=250$. The missing amount is £250.

questions.question_text:
A washing machine is £180 after a 60% reduction.
How much did it cost before the sale?

options.why: Adds a percentage amount instead of dividing by the remaining 40 percent.
Treats the sale price as if it were 75 percent of the original.
Calculates 40 percent of £180 rather than recovering the original price.

questions.solution_text: After a 60% reduction, £180 represents 40% of the original price. Thus original price is $180\div0.4=£450$.

questions.question_text:
There are 700 salmon in a pond.
This is an increase of 40% from last year.
How many salmon were in the pond last year?

options.why: Subtracts 40% of the current value rather than reversing the percentage increase.
Treats 40% as the fraction represented by the current total.
Subtracts an incorrect percentage amount from 700.

questions.solution_text: Let last year's number be $N$. Then $1.4N=700$, so $N=700/1.4=500$ salmon.

questions.question_text:
25% of a number is 8.
What is the original number?

options.why: This divides 8 by 4 instead of finding the whole.
This is not the exact result of reversing 25%.
This uses an incorrect multiplier for reversing 25%.

questions.solution_text:
$25\%$ is one quarter.
If one quarter is $8$, the whole is $8 \times 4 = 32$.

questions.question_text:
A jacket is £245 in the sale after a 30% reduction.
How much did the jacket cost before the sale?

options.why: Adds an approximate amount rather than reversing the 30 percent reduction.
Applies the 30 percent reduction to the sale price again.
Divides by an incorrect percentage multiplier.

questions.solution_text: After a 30% reduction, the sale price is 70% of the original. Therefore the original price is $245div0.7=£350$.
